construct: Osteoid osteoma is a small benign bone-forming tumor with a vascular osteoid nidus and surrounding reactive sclerosis; high local prostaglandin production contributes to severe nocturnal pain that characteristically responds to NSAIDs.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A teen with focal nocturnal pain dramatically relieved by NSAIDs plus a small cortical radiolucent nidus and reactive sclerosis has osteoid osteoma; osteoblastoma is larger and less classically NSAID-responsive.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Osteoblastoma shares osteoid production and can occur in young patients, but it is typically larger, often spinal, and pain is not classically relieved dramatically by NSAIDs; the small cortical nidus plus nocturnal NSAID-responsive pain uniquely favors osteoid osteoma.
